vulnerability_analysis: The BNRG token contract has a `launchRestrict` modifier that enforces rate limiting when state == Restricted. It requires both sender and recipient to not have transacted within the last 60 seconds (lastTx[addr].add(60) <= block.timestamp). After any transfer, it updates lastTx[sender] and lastTx[recipient] to block.timestamp. This creates a DoS vulnerability where an attacker can lock victim addresses by forcing transactions to/from them, preventing them from transacting for 60 seconds.
attack_strategy: 1. Enable Restricted mode via setBotProtection(true) as owner. 2. Inject BNRG tokens to attacker via storage manipulation. 3. Transfer tokens to victim address, which updates lastTx[victim] to block.timestamp. 4. Verify victim is now locked out (lastTx[victim] > block.timestamp - 60). This demonstrates the DoS vulnerability.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Get owner address and prank to enable Restricted mode. 2. Calculate storage slot for attacker's balance (balances mapping at slot 2). 3. Use vm.store() to inject 1000 BNRG tokens to attacker. 4. Call transfer() to send tokens to victim (this updates lastTx[victim]). 5. Load lastTx[victim] from storage (slot 9) and verify it's > block.timestamp - 60.
